greeting: Good morning, Rick! Amazon's Black Friday sale just kicked off, so pour that coffee and see what's worth a look.

items.title: White House says recent bank, FAA, Microsoft, and Apple outages were not an attack
items.note: After a string of big outages hit Microsoft, the FAA, Chase, and Apple, people wondered if the country was under cyberattack. The White House says no, each one had its own separate cause.

items.title: You Need to Download iOS 27.2.1 Now for These Security Fixes
items.note: Apple's iOS 27.2.1 update fixes nine issues, including a couple that could expose your personal data. Go to Settings, General, Software Update to grab it.

items.title: Amazon's 2026 Black Friday sale is now live
items.note: Amazon's official Black Friday sale is live and runs for 12 days, with deals on AirPods Pro 3, Apple Watch Series 12, TVs, and lots more. A good time to knock out some Christmas shopping early.

items.title: ChatGPT app gains enhanced Live Dictation streaming without 10-minute limit
items.note: ChatGPT's talk-to-type feature now shows your words as you speak and no longer cuts you off after 10 minutes. Handy if you'd rather talk than tap on your iPhone.

items.title: Ford Designed Its Fathom EV Battery Pack to Bend in a Crash, for Safety
items.note: Ford built the battery in its upcoming Fathom electric truck to bend in a crash and soak up side-impact force, instead of being babied like a fragile part. Ford says that makes the truck lighter and safer.

items.title: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
items.note: ULA says Sunday's Vulcan rocket failure came from a fuel supply problem, not the Blue Origin engines. That's a big relief for Blue Origin and NASA, since the same engines power the New Glenn rocket.

items.title: The iPhone Duo's hinge is wearing out after 525K folds in CNET's machine
items.note: CNET built a machine that has folded Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo more than 525,000 times in four weeks, and the hinge is finally starting to wear out. You can watch it live on YouTube.

items.title: 123456 is still the world's most common password
items.note: For the seventh time in eight years, 123456 is the world's most common password, with password and admin close behind in the US. A good nudge to check your own.
